author: Tamás Balog
html:
Regarding the ‘Promote Knowledge and Training’ section, I would add that commenting build configuration files can also be very useful, as they may get somewhat cryptic over time.

Add comment about why a certain thing is configured in a certain way, what performance benefits a given configuration is aimed to achieve, why certain dependencies are excluded, etc.

It can help with better understanding the config, and promote further optimization because people would know why things are done the way they are.

author: Brian Demers
html:
Absolutely Tamás!

Those comments help me future self (and co-workers) troubleshoot and deal with any potential dependency hell!😈

I’ve had cases were I’ve temporary added an extra dependency, and stuck a big “TODO: This dependency will not be needed in the future when the version of XYZ is updated to 1.2.3.”
That way a quick fix doesn’t stay around for ever!
